mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown a persistent downward trend over the last three weeks (0.4 -> 1.3 -> -0.6 -> -2.7), indicating momentum from accumulating caution/avoidance behavior that will continue to depress retail footfall over the next four weeks regardless of other series.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from 1.3 to -2.7 over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the mean over the last 28 days despite the three-week declining trend, indicating momentum does not persist.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week collapse in TRANSIT mobility signals the onset of formal movement restrictions or public transit curtailment, which mechanically reduces access to retail and recreation destinations within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from 3.0 to -3.0 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the two weeks following a TRANSIT drop exceeding 10 points, or rebounds to baseline despite continued TRANSIT suppression.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rises in GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL indicate a behavioral shift toward stockpiling essentials and staying home, substituting discretionary retail trips with grocery runs and in-home activity, which jointly suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 10% while RESIDENTIAL is non-negative in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose to 11.4 while RESIDENTIAL reached 0.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next 28 days even as GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated above 10% and RESIDENTIAL stays non-negative, refuting the substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of tightening restrictions, a slowing or reversing WORKPLACES trend (from 11.9 down to 9.7) signals reduced commuting and economic activity, which under lockdown conditions translates into lower incidental retail visits over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES declines for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from 11.9 to 11.6 to 9.7 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next two weeks despite WORKPLACES declining for two consecutive weeks, indicating decoupling of commuting and retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PARKS mobility (from 5.0 to -16.4 to -12.1) reflects reduced outdoor leisure activity, which is often co-located with nearby retail and recreation visits, so continued PARKS suppression will coincide with lower RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -10 in the latest week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell to -12.1 at t-0w after a steep drop from 5.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week immediately following a PARKS reading below -10, indicating no co-movement between outdoor leisure and retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES decline together, it indicates a coordinated lockdown-style suppression of both commuting and public transit use, compounding to produce a larger and more persistent decline in RETAIL_REC over four weeks than either series would predict alone.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both decline in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from 3.0 to -3.0 and WORKPLACES fell from 11.6 to 9.7 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decline over the next 28 days is no larger than predicted by TRANSIT or WORKPLACES declines individually, showing no compounding interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained spike in GROCERY_PHARM above 10% for two consecutive weeks signals panic-buying behavior that temporarily substitutes for broader discretionary retail activity; this substitution effect will keep RETAIL_REC suppressed until the GROCERY_PHARM spike subsides, within a two-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 10% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM measured 10.3 and 11.4 in the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds within two weeks even while GROCERY_PHARM remains above 10%, indicating no substitution relationship between grocery stockpiling and retail suppression.

mechanism_narrative: The gradual rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility from -1.6 to 0.0 over the snapshot period reflects an emerging seasonal/behavioral shift toward home-centered routines in mid-March, which structurally reduces time available for retail and recreation outings over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose steadily from -1.6 to 0.0 across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL continuing its upward trend toward or above zero, indicating no structural crowding-out effect from home-centered time use.
